To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the arginine transfer RNAsyntetase of Esch. coli is protected against heat denaturation by arginine and tRNASer but not by ATP.

the binding and the degree of protection against thermal denatuation given by transfer RNA to its arginine tRNA synthetase depend on the pH, the concentration of transfer RNA, and the concentration of arginine.
the arginine transfer RNAs synthetase of E. coli is protected against heat inactivation by its substrates, transfer RNAArg and arginine, but not by ATP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of arginine transfer RNA and its arginine with the enzyme arginine transfer RNA-synthetase of Escheichia coli.
the binding of arginine to its transfer RNA synthetases and the effects of this binding on the conformation of the protein.
the binding of transfer RNA to its amino acid synthetases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

arginine and t RNA Arg bind to the arginine t RNA synthetase in a manner that is dependent on the 3′ terminus of the transfer RNA and that this interaction is required to form a complex with arginine that is resistant to thermal inactivation.
the 3'-terminal adenosine of tRNAArg is essential for the catalysis of the reaction between tRNAArg and arginine but not for the binding of arginine to the synthetase.

the arginine transfer ribonucleic acid synthetase of E. coli is protected against heat denaturation by the binding of arginine and transfer ribonucleate acid, but that the binding of transfer ribonucleates acid alone requires higher concentrations at higher pH values, and that the binding of arginino-esterified transfer ribonucleatic acid is not as effective as that of arginine plus transfer ribonucleac acid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
arginine and tRNaArg bind to the arginine tRNA synthetase and protect it against thermal denatuation, and that arginine binds more tightly when the RNA is also bound.

the arginine binding site is a cleft in the enzyme that is formed by a number of amino acid residues and that the arginine transfer ribonucleic acid binding site is a shallow cleft that is formed by several amino acid residues and a phosphate group.

the arginine transfer RNAs synthetase is protected against thermal inactivation by arginine and transfer RNA, but the protection by transfer RNA is not due to a specific binding of the RNA but rather to a general effect of the RNA on the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arginine transfer RNA and arginyl-tRNA synthetase interact in a way that is different from that of other transfer RNAs and their synthetases.
the protection given to the arginine tRNA synthetase is not due to the formation of a ternary complex but is a consequence of the binding of transfer RNA and amino acid to the synthetase.
arginine is the primary ligand for the arginine tRNA synthetase and tRNAArg plays only an accessory role in the binding and protection of the enzyme.
